title: How Ghosts Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the question of how ghosts work, opening with Chuck's personal ghost story of seeing an elderly woman in a black robe and purple sash standing motionless in a Athens, Georgia intersection. They cover popular ghost photographs (Freddie Jackson, the Hanging Man of Oz, the Old West boothill photo, the girl in the fire), orbs in photos, why ghosts appear (delivering news, unfinished business, earthbound spirits, haunted hotels like the Hotel del Coronado), and theories of ghost composition (ectoplasm, energy, quantum particles and tunneling). They discuss researchers such as Richard Wiseman, paranormal psychology programs, and natural explanations including hallucinations, sleep paralysis, hypnagogic states, temperature changes and humidity, electromagnetic fields, the angular gyrus, magnetosphere, and infrasound (Vladimir Gavreau). The episode closes with a critique of the claim that belief in the paranormal reflects poor critical thinking, and a listener email about driving middle schoolers to Space Camp.

segments.title: Opening banter and Chuck's ghost story
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, reference a past horror fiction contest, and Chuck recounts seeing a motionless elderly woman in a black robe holding a Bible in an Athens, Georgia intersection, which he and a friend both saw.

segments.title: Belief in ghosts and the premise of the episode
segments.summary: The hosts note poll numbers on ghost belief, the difficulty of disproving ghosts, and that the episode will not conclusively declare ghosts nonexistent.

segments.title: Ghost photographs and fakes
segments.summary: They discuss famous ghost photos such as the Freddie Jackson photo, the Old West boothill photo, the girl by the fire, and a Google Earth image supposedly showing a murder that was later attributed to a dog, and how photos can be faked or explained.

segments.title: Why ghosts appear and haunted places
segments.summary: The hosts list reasons ghosts are said to appear, such as delivering news or being earthbound, and discuss haunted hotels including the Hotel del Coronado.

segments.title: Orbs in photographs
segments.summary: Orbs are discussed as supposed spirits, with Emily's photo of her dog and a grandfather orb, and skeptical explanations such as camera flash reflection, dust, and sensor defects.

segments.title: What ghosts are made of
segments.summary: Ectoplasm is mentioned as the Victorian idea, then the modern idea that ghosts are energy or quantum particles, with quantum tunneling discussed as a loose analogy.

segments.title: Paranormal research and Richard Wiseman
segments.summary: Richard Wiseman's study of reported sightings and physical conditions in haunted places is described, along with historical paranormal researchers like William James and Harry Price and university paranormal psychology programs.

segments.title: Natural explanations: hallucinations, cold spots, and EMF
segments.summary: Hallucinations, grief, sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic states are offered as explanations, along with temperature drops and humidity, electromagnetic fields, the angular gyrus, and the magnetosphere at night.

segments.title: Infrasound and ghostly effects
segments.summary: Infrasound is presented as a cause of dread and visual effects, referencing Vladimir Gavreau, a concert test, and a case where a fan's sound was linked to a haunting.

segments.title: Critical thinking and skepticism
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a claim that belief in the paranormal reduces critical thinking, and Brian Dunning's more open-minded skeptical approach.

segments.title: Listener mail: Space Camp car game
segments.summary: A middle school teacher describes driving students to Space Academy in Huntsville and a car game called pass around the ether rag.
